title: Knowledge check — 8 questions
note: Unlocks after the applied activity is submitted. Retakes are free and unlimited.

questions.prompt: Why must each column of the map come from an artifact rather than recall?
options: Because artifacts are easier to share with executives
Because self-report on time allocation is unreliable in a flattering direction — it understates Produce and overstates Decide
Because recall cannot produce percentages
Because artifacts are required for the Module 10 proposal
questions.explanation: Everyone who has read Module 2 can produce a plausible split in ninety seconds, and it will be wrong predictably: Produce is unglamorous and Decide is what we'd like to be doing.

questions.prompt: What does a calendar systematically over- and under-count?
options: Over-counts Produce; under-counts Decide
Over-counts Verify; under-counts Sense
Over-counts Decide and Distribute because those generate meetings; under-counts Produce because drafting happens in the gaps and never appears as an entry
It counts all six links evenly, which is why it's the preferred instrument
questions.explanation: Every instrument has a known distortion, and the choice matters less than the labelling. An acknowledged estimate is usable; a confident invention is not.

questions.prompt: Why should someone who leads a team map the team rather than themselves?
options: Because team data is more accurate than individual data
Because a director's week is mostly Decide, so mapping it shows a healthy function over a team doing nothing but Produce
Because individual maps cannot be compared across organizations
Because headcount and budget are team-level figures anyway
questions.explanation: The map is of the function, not the mapper. This is the distortion that catches people who are otherwise doing the exercise carefully.

questions.prompt: How should link ownership be established?
options: By asking who spends the most time on it
By asking who has the relevant skills
By asking whose performance review is affected if the link fails — a question whose only acceptable answer is a person's name
By checking the org chart
questions.explanation: Touching a link is not owning it. And work that appears in nobody's review is work that stops happening the first busy month, which is why "nobody" is the most important answer this column can produce.

questions.prompt: What is the most common gap between the time column and the budget column?
options: Time in Decide, money in Produce
Time in Produce, money in Distribute — the financial lever pointed at the link that was mostly solved before AI, with no budget line against Sense or Interpret
Time in Distribute, money in Verify
Time and money both concentrate in Produce
questions.explanation: The function spends its hours making things and its budget on the platform that delivers them. That sentence with your own numbers in it is the strongest single line in a Module 10 proposal.

questions.prompt: Why is proofreading classified as Produce rather than Verify?
options: Because it is performed by the same person who drafts
Because it happens before publication rather than after
Because it is quality control on the artifact — Verify asks whether what was published was true, and whether it landed
Because it is too small a task to constitute its own link
questions.explanation: Teams that log proofreading as Verify produce maps showing healthy verification coverage over a function that has never once asked whether a message worked. It is the single most common error in this exercise.

questions.prompt: A team has heavy Produce and Distribute, a significant platform budget, sophisticated segmentation, and no owner at Sense. Which shape is it, and what follows?
options: The production shop — start with Verify
The broadcast desk — the Sense capability is a report away rather than a purchase away, because the platform already captures the data
The two-person function — use the map as evidence for headcount
The embedded advisor — the sampling problem is the priority
questions.explanation: Most modern communication platforms capture search and engagement data nobody in the function reads. This shape already owns the instrument and isn't using it.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest argument *against* building a compression map at all?
options: That six links is too granular to measure reliably
That mandates are won through relationships and crises rather than analysis — and a map showing 70% of time in the collapsing link is evidence for the prosecution, self-produced
That the data required is not available in most organizations
That executives prefer qualitative narratives to functional maps
questions.explanation: It is a genuinely strong counter and the module says so. Whether it holds depends entirely on who would receive the document in your organization, which is why the activity asks you to name them.
